summary: Tutorial (Artist track) for surface-dependent footstep audio: randomized Sound Cues per surface, Physical Materials, a PrimaryDataAsset mapping Physical Material to Sound Cue, a function-library function that line traces down and plays the sound, triggered from AnimNotify FootPlant events in the Animation Blueprint and Event On Landed.
gotchas: Set Variable Type before choosing Map container; booleans cannot be mapped so Map is unavailable on the default type
Compile the Blueprint before editing variable default values
Every Animation Blueprint the character uses needs the notify logic added
Physical Material can be set per actor via Collision > Phys Material Override or on a Material Instance (General > Phys Material)

summary: Tutorial (Artist track) on Niagara basics: create a system from the Hanging Particulates emitter, build a translucent unlit SubUV fire material, make a Minimal Lightweight (stateless) emitter fire, add it as a Niagara component to a trap Blueprint, toggle it with Activate/Deactivate and drive a User Parameter from the Construction Script.
gotchas: Lightweight (stateless) emitters perform better but support only a limited set of modules
Set Niagara Variable In Variable Name must match the Niagara user parameter name exactly
Sub Image Size must match the SubUV texture grid (6x6 here)
Add the Niagara component as a child of the base component so it scales with it

summary: Section 1 of the C++ First Person Shooter tutorial: create a Blank C++ project, set the Editor Startup Map, open it in Visual Studio, override AGameModeBase::StartPlay to print an on-screen debug message, compile, derive a Blueprint from the C++ Game Mode and set it as Default GameMode.
keys: Create Blueprint class based on FPSProjectGameModeBase
gotchas: Code samples assume the project is named FPSProject
The log message does not appear until the project's Default GameMode is set to the new Game Mode

summary: Reference for Blueprint flow-control nodes with pin tables: Switch on Int/String/Name/Enum and editing their pins, plus Branch, DoN, DoOnce, FlipFlop, ForLoop, ForLoopWithBreak, Gate, MultiGate, Sequence and WhileLoop with examples.
gotchas: Removing a pin on Switch on Int shifts higher-valued pins down by 1
Large ForLoops can incur a performance hit
Sequence outputs fire in order with no delay, appearing simultaneous
WhileLoop without an updated terminating condition causes an infinite loop that can hang or crash the game

summary: Explains Blueprint node basics: placing nodes from the context menu, selecting and moving, execution vs data pins, auto-casting, Promote to Variable, exec/data wires and how to make or break them, and collapsing nodes into sub-graphs with tunnel nodes.
gotchas: Collapsed graphs are not shared; copying one duplicates the internal graph so fixes must be applied to each copy
Alt + Click on a pin breaks its wires

summary: How to add node comments and comment boxes in Blueprint graphs, edit or delete them, and set comment box properties (color, bubble, move mode).
gotchas: Press C to create a comment box, F2 to edit
Moving a comment box moves enclosed nodes unless Move Mode is changed
Node comments do not scale with zoom; comment box text does

summary: Explains Blueprint Functions: Public/Protected/Private access specifiers, Pure vs Impure (BlueprintPure/BlueprintCallable), creating functions in Blueprints and Interfaces, adding input/output parameters, calling them locally or from another Blueprint via a cast, and fixing 'Unable to find function' warnings.
keys: Unable to find function with name
gotchas: Pure functions run once per connected node
Functions can only have data inputs/outputs, unlike macros
Recompile after changing a function's number of inputs or outputs or when the call node shows a Warning bar

summary: Describes the per-level Level Blueprint event graph: opening it from the Blueprints toolbar button, creating references to placed Actors, and adding Actor events; notes the default Level Blueprint class is set in DefaultGame.ini.
gotchas: New Level Blueprints cannot be created through the editor; each level has exactly one by default

summary: How to create and build Blueprint Macros with Inputs/Outputs tunnel nodes, add exec and data pins, set Description/Category/Instance Color, and place macro nodes in graphs.
gotchas: Unlike functions, macros can have multiple output execution pins or none

summary: Describes the Blueprint Editor's My Blueprint panel: its sections (Graphs, Functions, Macros, Variables, Event Dispatchers), creation buttons for each, which items appear per Blueprint type, and searching within the Blueprint.

Overview comparing ways Actors share information in Blueprint/C++: direct references, casting, interfaces (UInterface) and delegates/Event Dispatchers, with when-to-use guidance, a reference table and links to each quick start guide.
gotchas: Direct, casting and interface calls all need a reference to the target Actor
Event Dispatcher listeners must subscribe (bind) to react

summary: How to add and remove events from an Event Dispatcher with Bind Event, Unbind Event and Unbind All Events nodes, in Blueprint Classes and Level Blueprints.
gotchas: Calling a dispatcher with no bound events does nothing
Each event binds only once even if Bind runs repeatedly
Unbind All Events in the Blueprint Class unbinds for all instances, in the Level Blueprint only for the given Target

summary: How a Blueprint implements a Blueprint or C++ interface: sample UINTERFACE C++ code, adding/removing it under Class Settings > Implemented Interfaces, implementing functions, overriding a BlueprintNativeEvent with Add Call to Parent Function, and the Object/Interface/Message call node variants.
gotchas: Message calls fail silently if the object lacks the interface and are slower than Object/Interface calls
BlueprintImplementableEvent can only be implemented in Blueprint; BlueprintNativeEvent in Blueprint, C++ or both
Blueprint implementations override parent implementations by default

summary: Reference for Blueprint Editor toolbar buttons: compile states, Save, Find in Content Browser, Search, Class Settings/Defaults, Simulate, Play, Pause/Resume/Frame Skip, Stop, Possess/Eject, Step, and the debug instance dropdown.
gotchas: Compile button is inactive during debugging

summary: Explains writing C++ Blueprint Function Libraries: classes deriving from UBlueprintFunctionLibrary holding static UFUNCTION utility methods (BlueprintCallable or BlueprintPure), with Analytics and AI helper library examples.
gotchas: Library classes should contain only static methods
Frequently called logic in C++ outperforms the equivalent Blueprint function

summary: How to create a Blueprint Macro Library asset (Blueprints > Blueprint Macro Library with a Parent Class) to share macros project-wide, plus building macros with tunnel pins and placing them in other graphs.
gotchas: Macro libraries need no compile, but changes reach referencing graphs only after those Blueprints recompile
Macros are expanded inline at compile time

summary: How to debug Blueprints during PIE/SIE: choosing the Debug Object instance, adding/disabling/enabling Breakpoints, watching pin values, and using the Debug window's Watch Window, Call Stack and Execution Trace.
gotchas: Breakpoints are saved in project .ini files and persist between sessions
A yellow breakpoint with ! is invalid and never hit; recompiling may fix it
Pins show no value until their node has executed at least once
Macros do not appear in the Call Stack; PrintScriptCallstack works only in editor builds

summary: Step-by-step for consolidating selected Blueprint nodes via Collapse Nodes, Collapse to Function or Collapse to Macro, adding exec/data pins to the result, and reverting with Expand Node.
gotchas: Only a collapsed Function can be called from another Blueprint (given a reference)

summary: Ways to wire Blueprint nodes: pin-to-pin with automatic conversion nodes, pin action shortcuts (break/move connections), swapping variable Get/Set nodes by dropping another variable on them, drag-and-drop variables onto pins, and Reroute nodes.
gotchas: Alt + Left-Click on a pin breaks all its connections; Ctrl + drag moves them to another pin

summary: Beginner walkthrough: make an Actor Blueprint that enables input on Event Begin Play via Get Player Controller/Enable Input, create a Print Text function using Print String, and call it from an F key event.
gotchas: If the new function does not appear in search, Compile the Blueprint first

summary: How to add Blueprint nodes: drag variables (Get/Set), functions, macros and Event Dispatchers from My Blueprint, use the right-click Context Menu with the Context Sensitive filter, drag off pins for filtered actions, and keyboard shortcuts.
gotchas: Context Sensitive filtering is on by default and can hide nodes; uncheck it to see everything

summary: Explains primitive vs object reference variables and builds a TriggerBox teleporter Blueprint: Actor-type variables, Get/Set nodes, Set Actor Location with Teleport on ActorBeginOverlap, and assigning a reference per instance in the Details panel.
gotchas: Object variables are only references; setting them does not create or replace objects
Using empty (unset) references throws an error at runtime
Click the eye icon to make a variable editable per instance in the Details panel

summary: Short conceptual overview of a Blueprint Class: Components, the Construction Script and EventGraph graphs, and reusing script via Functions, Macros and collapsed graphs.

Guidance on structuring Blueprints: avoid heavy per-tick math (use C++), Level Blueprints vs Blueprint Classes, class vs local variables, functions vs macros (latent nodes, overriding, multiple exec pins), communication types, and editor/graph organization tips.
gotchas: Heavy operations and complex math every tick are better in native C++
Latent nodes (e.g. delays) can be used in macros but not in functions
Functions can be overridden in child Blueprints and targeted on other objects; macros cannot

summary: When-to-use guide for Blueprint communication: direct references, Event Dispatchers (one-to-many notifications like a boss OnDied), Blueprint Interfaces (shared contract like OnTakeWeaponFire) and Cast nodes (accessing a specialized subclass), with gameplay examples.
gotchas: A Cast fails if the object is not of the target class, so its functions are inaccessible
Objects not implementing an interface simply ignore the call

summary: Reference for the Blueprint Debugger window (Tools or Blueprint Editor Debug menu): breakpoints, watches and hover tooltips during PIE/SIE, the Data Flow tab with object filtering, Call Stack and Execution Trace.
gotchas: Breakpoints persist in the project's .ini files but are not shared with other developers
Yellow ! breakpoints are invalid and never reached; recompiling may fix
Pins have no debug value until their node executes once
Macros do not appear in the Call Stack; PrintScriptCallstack only in editor builds

summary: Keyboard and mouse shortcut tables for the Blueprint Editor: selection, graph navigation, generic commands (compile, find), variable drag actions, node actions (breakpoints, duplicate, comment), pin actions and key+click shortcuts for creating common nodes.
gotchas: Ctrl + LMB drag a variable into the graph makes a Get; Alt + LMB drag makes a Set

summary: How to create a Blueprint Interface asset and define its function signatures (inputs, outputs, defaults, ordering) with no implementation, so disparate Blueprints can share calls like OnTakeWeaponFire.
gotchas: Blueprint Interfaces cannot add variables, edit graphs or add components
Interface functions have no implementation; implementing Blueprints define behavior

summary: Explains Blueprint Namespaces, which defer loading Blueprint Function/Macro Library assets and filter context-menu actions: setting a Blueprint Namespace in Class Settings, importing namespaces explicitly, via Namespaces to Always Include in Editor Preferences/Project Settings, or implicitly, and filtering non-imported types.
gotchas: Namespace settings sit under Experimental categories in Editor Preferences and Project Settings
Namespace strings cannot contain characters like # or ,
Project Settings changes apply to every user on source control; Editor Preferences are per-user
Aimed at load-time savings in large projects

summary: How to create an Event Dispatcher in the My Blueprint panel, add typed inputs (or Copy Signature from another event), and use its event, bind, unbind and call nodes in a Blueprint Class versus the Level Blueprint.
gotchas: The Event Dispatcher's own graph is locked and cannot be edited
Target defaults to Self in the class (affects every instance); in the Level Blueprint it needs a specific instance reference

summary: Conceptual intro to Blueprint Visual Scripting: node graphs, Level Blueprints vs Blueprint Classes, and what Blueprints are used for (Construction Script prefabs, playable Pawn/Character, HUD), with links to the Blueprint Editor and tutorials.
gotchas: The Construction Script runs when an actor is placed or updated in the editor, not during gameplay
UMG is recommended over a Blueprint HUD class for UI layout

summary: First-Blueprint walkthrough: build a launchpad Actor from Cube and Box Collision components, convert it with Blueprint/Add Script, and on OnComponentBeginOverlap compare Other Actor to Get Player Pawn, Branch, Cast to Character and call Launch Character.
gotchas: Launch Character only works on Characters, so the Pawn must be cast first
Uses the Side Scroller Blueprint template with Starter Content

summary: Hub page for the 'Your First Hour' video course building a small 3D platformer: links to six modules covering install/project creation, an Enhanced Input flashlight, a coin pickup Blueprint, a UMG HUD, a game over screen and packaging.
gotchas: Requires Unreal Engine 5.3 or above

summary: Hub page for the Artist Track tutorial series on the Puzzle Adventure project: lists modules on importing content, lighting, materials and instances, post process volumes and materials, environment lighting, fire trap sounds, MetaSounds music, footstep sounds and Niagara VFX, with example project downloads.
gotchas: Some steps require the project state from the Design a Puzzle Adventure Game track

summary: Designer track module 1: create a First Person (Arena Shooter variant) project and Basic level, set Editor Startup Map and Game Default Map, test with PIE/Standalone/Quick Launch, then grey-box a level with LevelPrototyping meshes using scale guidelines (cm units, human 1.8m), grid snapping, Blocking Volumes, Outliner folders, Text Render Actors and copy-paste text snippets of the sample blockout.
gotchas: Restart the editor if assets or actors fail to appear or update, since UE relies heavily on caching
Never place blocking volumes where players expect to move freely
Scale spaces about 1.5x for third-person cameras
Paste the blockout snippets into a Basic level with Floor and PlayerStart deleted, with the viewport or Outliner focused
